source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, Swine Health Management, Volume 2: Guide to Prevent and Control Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012)
text: Simple farmer-facing rules for PRRS prevention and control: Report sick or dying pigs to the local veterinary or agriculture authority right away — early detection allows early control. Only buy healthy animals from sources known to be disease-free, and be cautious of animals sold at unusually low prices, since this can be a sign they are sick. Keep any newly purchased pig separate from the rest of the herd for 30 days before mixing them together. Limit contact between your pigs and visitors, especially traders. Avoid visiting other pig farms, particularly if there is news of disease in the area. If feeding swill, cook it for at least one hour at 100°C before giving it to pigs. Use your own clean farm equipment rather than borrowing tools from neighboring farms. Regularly clean pens and disinfect empty pens before bringing in new animals. Never sell, buy, or move sick pigs — this is one of the fastest ways disease spreads between farms. Never sell a dead pig; always burn or bury animals that died from disease.
